video.transcriptSummary: This live 45-second case study demonstrates the complete Antigravity Enterprise Product Video Playbook in action. Every frame was built as deterministic, version-controlled code in Remotion (60 fps), powered by real brand tokens, native 60 fps hardware-GPU Playwright gameplay captures driven by a zero-collision closed-loop autopilot, synthesized FFmpeg trailer SFX, exact millisecond beat-locking to the theme song's 'HEY!' chorus hits, keyframe contact-sheet visual QA, and broadcast -14 LUFS loudness mastering for simultaneous 16:9 widescreen and 9:16 vertical exports.

steps.title: The Hybrid 4-Layer Code-as-Video Architecture
steps.summary: Pure text-to-video AI hallucinates UI text and drifts off-brand, while raw screen recordings feel static and break every time your UI changes. Pro enterprise teams run one deterministic Code-as-Video timeline (Remotion + Playwright + FFmpeg) fed by four hybrid media layers.
keyTakeaways: Layer 1 — Programmatic Motion Graphics (Remotion / SVG): Pixel-sharp UI callouts, progressive architecture diagrams, kinetic headlines, lower thirds, and intros locked to exact brand tokens.
Layer 2 — Directed Product Capture (Playwright): Clean, high-DPI, privacy-safe product walkthroughs with 100% synthetic demo data and zero messy browser chrome.
Layer 3 — Selective Generative Visuals (Gemini API Veo / Imagen): 2–4 second conceptual cutaways, abstract backdrops, and editorial metaphors — never used for readable UI text or charts.
Layer 4 — Broadcast Audio Stack (VO + SFX + FFmpeg): Locked narration or soundtrack with word/beat timestamps driving frame numbers, subtle micro-SFX (-18 to -24 dB), and -14 LUFS loudness mastering.

Beginner Superpower: With Antigravity as your operator, you direct like a Creative Director (reviewing briefs, keyframes, and live browser previews) while Antigravity authors and updates the modular scene code.
actionChecklist: Choose a single timeline engine (Remotion) rather than juggling two parallel editors.
Verify local prerequisites: Node.js, pnpm, FFmpeg, and a cached Chromium binary for Playwright.
Classify every scene in your upcoming video into one of the four media layers before generating a single asset.

steps.title: Step 0: Reusable Studio Workspace & Brand-Token Lock
steps.summary: Build a reusable product-video-studio repository once so every future video inherits your exact brand palette, licensed fonts, damped spring physics, and export presets automatically—eliminating visual drift across 50+ enterprise videos.
keyTakeaways: Organize cleanly into brand/ (brand-bible.md, tokens.ts, vector logos, fonts), plans/ (<slug>-spec.json), scripts/ (capture-gameplay.mjs, generate-sfx.sh, master-export.sh), src/components/, src/scenes/, and out/.
Lock your Color Architecture in brand/tokens.ts: 1 dark or light canvas, 1 surface elevation, 1 high-contrast active accent, and WCAG 4.5:1 text tokens.

Ban linear easing: standardize damped Remotion spring presets (SNAPPY damping 18 / stiffness 190 for UI; CINEMATIC damping 24 / stiffness 95 for camera pans; SLAM damping 13 / stiffness 240 for title punches).
Enforce an Anti-Cliché Rule in brand-bible.md: ban generic stock tropes (handshakes, glowing blue AI brains, floating HUDs) in favor of authentic product visuals and original visual metaphors.
actionChecklist: Create a dedicated product-video-studio/ workspace and install Remotion, React, TypeScript, QRCode, and Playwright (all MIT/Apache-2.0).
Extract exact hex palette and font files from your real product repository into brand/tokens.ts and public/fonts/.
Define reusable primitives (FilmGrainOverlay, StampBadge, DeviceMockup, QrCodeCard) before authoring individual scenes.

steps.title: Steps 1–2: Narrative Architecture & Machine-Readable Storyboard
steps.summary: Enterprise product videos fail when they recite features in menu order. Use /grill-me to lock a 1-page Creative Brief, apply the Zoom-In / Zoom-Out storytelling arc, write lean scripts for the ear, and compile a machine-readable JSON storyboard before animating.
keyTakeaways: Lock 4 decisions upfront: Single Target Audience (C-suite vs. Architect vs. End User), One Core Transformation, Runtime Budget (45s teaser / 90–120s hero explainer / 3–5m walkthrough), and Distribution Targets.

Use the 5-Act Zoom-In / Zoom-Out Arc: 1. Friction Hook (0–12s, zero 8-second logo intros) -> 2. Mental Model / Visual Metaphor (12–30s) -> 3. Concrete Product Proof (30–75s) -> 4. Enterprise Trust & Scale (75–95s) -> 5. Clear CTA (95–110s).
Apply the Progressive Disclosure Rule: never drop a 20-box architecture diagram on screen all at once—reveal 1 node per beat, animate data flow to the next node, and dim inactive context.

Write for the ear (135–150 WPM, max 16 words per sentence) and obey 'Show, Don't Duplicate' (5–7 on-screen words max per card). Lock plans/<slug>-spec.json and preview style frames before coding scenes.
actionChecklist: Run /grill-me with Antigravity to lock audience, transformation, runtime, and tone in a 1-page Creative Brief.
Write a spoken-word script under your WPM ceiling (e.g., <= 220 words for a 90s explainer; <= 80 words for a 45s teaser).
Compile plans/<video-slug>-spec.json with explicit scene IDs, frame ranges, visual layers, camera motions, and SFX cues.

steps.title: Step 3: Audio-First Production & Exact Frame-Level Beat Sync
steps.summary: Amateur editors animate first and cram audio underneath. Pro editors lock the voiceover and/or soundtrack first, extract exact word and beat timestamps, and convert milliseconds directly into Remotion frame numbers so every jump, cut, and headline lands on the exact syllable.
keyTakeaways: Lock your VO (studio recording or neural speech via Gemini API / ElevenLabs) or hero soundtrack BEFORE assembling visuals.
Extract word-level timestamps (Whisper/Gemini transcription -> captions.json) and musical onset energy peaks (via FFmpeg + Python RMS) to build a deterministic beat map.
Convert audio timestamps to exact timeline frames: const impactFrame = Math.round(((songHitSec - songOffsetSec) * fps));.

Case Study Proof: In the Herd of Ibiza teaser above, RMS analysis pinpointed 'HEY!' #1 at 46.75s and 'HEY!' #2 at 49.05s (2.300s apart), letting us align both live alpaca jumps within 3 milliseconds (0.2 frames) of the vocals.
Keep SFX understated (-18 to -24 dB) and clear of key vocal hooks so sound design elevates polish without fighting narration or lyrics.
actionChecklist: Lock your master VO or soundtrack slice (e.g., setting soundtrackStartSeconds so the chorus hits your hero product climax).
Run a quick FFmpeg + Python RMS onset script or transcription pass to record exact beat/word timestamps.
Define named frame constants (e.g., HEY_1_FRAME, HEY_2_FRAME) in your scenes so visuals, beat rings, and SFX share one clock.

codeSnippet.code:
import subprocess, struct, math

cmd = [
    "ffmpeg", "-v", "error", "-ss", "40", "-t", "15",
    "-i", "public/music/theme.mp3", "-ac", "1", "-ar", "16000", "-f", "s16le", "-"
]
raw = subprocess.check_output(cmd)
samples = struct.unpack(f"<{len(raw)//2}h", raw)
win = 800  # 50ms windows @ 16kHz
for i in range(0, len(samples) - win, win):
    rms = math.sqrt(sum(s*s for s in samples[i:i+win]) / win) / 32768.0
    if rms > 0.35:
        print(f"{40.0 + i/16000:6.2f}s | energy={rms:.3f}")

steps.title: Step 4: Butter-Smooth 60fps UI Capture & Pro Autopilot Scripting
steps.summary: Default headless browser recordings look jerky because software WebGL (SwiftShader) crawls at ~6 fps and Playwright's built-in recordVideo caps at 25 fps. Pro Code-as-Video capture uses hardware GPU acceleration, native 60 fps canvas streaming, and closed-loop scripting so your product looks like a world-class expert is operating it.
keyTakeaways: Always enable hardware GPU acceleration (e.g., --use-gl=angle --use-angle=metal on Apple Silicon) instead of software SwiftShader.
For ultra-smooth 60 fps product/WebGL footage, capture directly via canvas.captureStream(60) + MediaRecorder (VP9 @ 12–14 Mbps) and transcode to constant-60fps H.264 with FFmpeg.
Run all setup, login, and synthetic enterprise data seeding BEFORE recording begins—zero loading spinners, zero mid-clip teleports, and zero customer PII.

Never drive demos with blind timers that look like a confused newbie clicking around: build a closed-loop Playwright script (or autopilot) that reads live app state, hits targets cleanly, and asserts zero errors/collisions before saving the clip.
actionChecklist: Verify your browser reports hardware GPU rendering and ~60 rAF FPS before recording.
Seed realistic, 100% synthetic enterprise demo data (no real customer names, tokens, or 'test123' placeholders).
Add automated post-capture assertions (zero console errors, zero UI glitches, expected state transitions achieved) to your capture script.

steps.title: Step 5: Pro Editing Craft, Motion Polish & FFmpeg Audio Mastering
steps.summary: Stacking slides in sequence creates a PowerPoint; applying editorial rhythm, audio bridges, spring choreography, and broadcast loudness normalization turns code into cinema.
keyTakeaways: The 3-to-5 Second Visual Beat Rule: shift something meaningful every 3–5 seconds (zoom to control, highlight diagram node, switch camera angle, slam a callout badge). Never hold a dead static screen for 10+ seconds.
J-Cuts & L-Cuts: start the next scene's audio riser or VO 0.25–0.45s before the visual cut so scene transitions flow cinematically.

Staggered Choreography & Safe Margins: stagger multi-element entrances by 4–6 frames (at 60 fps) with damped springs, and keep every critical label inside 8–10% title-safe margins with >= 4.5:1 contrast.

Broadcast FFmpeg Mastering: normalize integrated loudness to -14 LUFS (YouTube/web) or -16 LUFS (LMS/mobile) with true peak <= -1.0 dBTP, sidechain-duck music -18 to -22 dB under voiceover, and always write +faststart so web videos play instantaneously.
actionChecklist: Audit every scene length against the 3–5 second visual beat rule and add J-cut audio bridges where cuts feel abrupt.
Build responsive layouts in the same Remotion components (isVertical = height > width) so 16:9 and 9:16 reflow cleanly without awkward cropping.
Run scripts/master-export.sh with FFmpeg loudnorm + faststart and verify the printed Integrated LUFS and True Peak metrics.

steps.title: Steps 6–7: Keyframe Contact-Sheet QA & Enterprise Localization Scale
steps.summary: Never render a 4K master blind. Run a deterministic visual QA contact sheet across every act before final encode, pass the silent-autoplay test, and unlock one-command quarterly UI refreshes and global multi-language renders.
keyTakeaways: Keyframe Contact-Sheet Audit: render PNG stills at the midpoint and climax of every scene with `remotion still` and inspect them in Antigravity to catch clipped labels, divider overlaps, sheen box edges, or wrong capture trim offsets in 15 seconds instead of after a 5-minute encode.

Silent-Autoplay Test: watch the entire export muted—over 70% of LinkedIn, Slack, and enterprise portal viewers first encounter video without sound, so visuals + captions must tell the complete story alone.
Zero-Rework Quarterly Maintenance: when your product UI ships a redesign, re-run scripts/capture-gameplay.mjs and re-render—all timing, motion graphics, voiceovers, and music mixes stay intact.

One-Command Multi-Language Localization: because copy lives in JSON/props and visuals are React components, translating a launch video into Spanish, German, or Japanese is just swapping the localized strings + VO track and letting Remotion re-render every scene cleanly.
actionChecklist: Render a 1-still-per-scene contact sheet with `remotion still` and visually inspect every frame before running full MP4 renders.
Verify zero confidential data, real API keys, customer PII, or unlicensed media assets appear in any clip.
Export the full enterprise distribution matrix: 16:9 master, web-light 1080p embed, 9:16 vertical social cutdown, and .vtt/.srt caption sidecars.

prompts.title: Stage 1–2: Creative Brief & Machine-Readable Storyboard
prompts.description: Interview stakeholders to lock audience, transformation, runtime, Zoom-In/Zoom-Out narrative arc, and a frame-accurate JSON storyboard spec before building a single scene.
prompts.template:
Act as a Senior Enterprise Video Creative Director. We are building a {{runtime_seconds}}-second product video for {{product_name}} aimed at {{audience}}.

1. Interview me (max 5 crisp questions) to lock the single core transformation, visual tone ({{visual_style}}), and live product proof points.
2. Draft a spoken-word script written for the ear (<= 145 WPM, sentences <= 16 words) using the 5-act Zoom-In / Zoom-Out structure.
3. Compile a locked machine-readable storyboard at `plans/{{video_slug}}-spec.json` with exact 60fps frame ranges, visual layers (Remotion diagram / Playwright capture / AI metaphor), on-screen headlines (<= 7 words), camera motions, and SFX cues.
4. Do not render or scaffold code until I approve the storyboard.

prompts.expectedOutcome: Produces a locked 1-page Creative Brief, ear-first script, and machine-readable plans/<video_slug>-spec.json ready for parallel production.

prompts.title: Step 0: Scaffold Reusable Code-as-Video Studio
prompts.description: Initialize a clean Remotion + Playwright + FFmpeg studio repository locked to your product's real color palette, fonts, spring physics, and 16:9 + 9:16 responsive compositions.
prompts.template:
Scaffold a reusable Code-as-Video studio at `{{studio_path}}` using Remotion (60 fps), TypeScript, Playwright, QRCode, and FFmpeg (MIT/Apache-2.0 only).

1. Inspect `{{product_repo_path}}` (read-only) and extract the real brand hex palette, font files, logos, and assets into `brand/tokens.ts`, `brand/brand-bible.md`, and `public/`.
2. Create reusable motion primitives (`FontLoader`, `FilmGrainOverlay`, `StampBadge`, `QrCodeCard`) using damped spring physics (no linear easing) and WCAG 4.5:1 contrast inside 10% title-safe zones.
3. Register both responsive `16x9` (1920x1080) and `9x16` (1080x1920) compositions in `src/Root.tsx` plus an FFmpeg `-14 LUFS` + `+faststart` mastering script at `scripts/master-export.sh`.
4. Ask for my approval before installing npm dependencies.
prompts.expectedOutcome: Creates a typechecked, brand-locked Code-as-Video studio ready to render both 16:9 and 9:16 masters.

prompts.title: Step 4: 60fps Hardware-GPU Pro UI Capture Script
prompts.description: Build a Playwright script using hardware Metal/WebGL acceleration and closed-loop state awareness so product footage looks like an expert operator—zero stutter, zero PII, zero fumbles.
prompts.template:
Write `scripts/capture-product.mjs` to capture silky-smooth 60 fps product clips from `{{app_url}}` for scenes `{{scene_list}}`.

Requirements:
1. Launch Chromium with hardware GPU acceleration (`--use-gl=angle --use-angle=metal` on macOS, never software SwiftShader) and verify ~60 rAF FPS.
2. Seed 100% synthetic enterprise demo data and finish all navigation BEFORE recording begins (zero loading spinners or teleports in the clip).
3. Use smooth, closed-loop interactions (reading live DOM/app state rather than blind timeouts) and record at native 60 fps (`canvas.captureStream(60)` for WebGL or high-DPI viewport capture).
4. Log exact millisecond timestamps of key hero interactions into `public/clips/clip-metadata.json` and assert zero console errors or failed interactions before exiting.
prompts.expectedOutcome: Produces smooth 60/1 fps H.264 clips in public/clips/ plus clip-metadata.json with exact interaction timestamps.

prompts.title: Step 3: Audio Beat-Map & Frame-Exact Sync
prompts.description: Analyze your soundtrack or voiceover to find exact millisecond peaks and align hero visual cuts, jumps, and title slams within 1 frame of the audio.
prompts.template:
Analyze `{{audio_file}}` using FFmpeg + Python RMS onset detection (and/or word-level transcription) to locate exact timestamps for the key vocal hooks or beat drops around `{{target_window_sec}}`.

1. Choose the optimal `soundtrackStartSeconds` offset so the main chorus or vocal hook lands directly on our hero product climax scene (`{{climax_scene}}`).
2. Compute exact 60 fps frame numbers (`Math.round((hitSec - startSec) * 60)`) and wire them into `src/compositions/` and the climax scene so visual impacts, beat rings, and transitions fire on the exact syllable.
3. Keep micro-SFX subtle (-18 to -24 dB) and clear of vocals so lyrics/narration stay crystal clear.
prompts.expectedOutcome: Locks visual impacts and gameplay action directly to exact audio frames with broadcast-clean mix balance.

prompts.title: Step 6: Keyframe Contact-Sheet Visual QA & Master Render
prompts.description: Render PNG stills at the midpoint and climax of every scene, audit them visually for overlaps, contrast, and capture timing, fix defects, and master 16:9 + 9:16 exports to -14 LUFS.
prompts.template:
Run a full pre-master Visual QA pass on `{{composition_id}}` before encoding the final MP4s:

1. Run `pnpm run typecheck` and render PNG keyframes at the midpoint and impact frame of every scene into `out/qa-frames/` using `remotion still`.
2. Visually inspect EVERY rendered PNG for text overlap, clipped borders, contrast < 4.5:1, safe-margin violations, unintended menu frames inside UI clips, or shader/gradient edge artifacts.
3. Fix all defects, re-verify the affected stills, then render both `16:9` and `9:16` H.264 masters and normalize audio to `-14 LUFS` / `-1.0 dBTP` with `+faststart` via `scripts/master-export.sh`.
prompts.expectedOutcome: Catches layout and capture bugs before full encode and produces verified -14 LUFS 16:9 and 9:16 masters.
